title: Deferred-preference spend pacer for burst and steady-state routing
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: sudden shifts between spot and on-demand routing cause cost oscillations and customer QoS blips during bursts. We need a pacing controller that smooths region/tier preference changes over time, enforces windowed soft+hard budget caps per-tenant, and preserves SLOs by reserving minimal GPU-class headroom and fallback model variants when necessary.

Proposal summary: Implement a deferred-preference spend pacer in the routing layer that: (1) applies a time-windowed spend budget (e.g., 5m rolling) with soft throttles and hard caps, (2) uses a decaying preference score for spot vs on-demand to avoid flip-flopping on short price/availability signals, (3) reserves configurable GPU-class headroom (e.g., 10% for on-demand) when nearing caps to reduce eviction risk, and (4) integrates graceful fallback to pre-approved model variants (quantized or lower-capacity variants) with staged degradation rather than abrupt failures. The pacer exposes telemetry and per-tenant knobs via the console and supports feature flags for canary rollout.

Why different from existing routers: instead of immediate price-based bidding or single-step fallbacks, this approach explicitly models temporal smoothing, windowed budgets, and GPU-class reservation as first-class concepts to optimize for both cost and application-level stability.
acceptance_criteria: Routing applies 5-minute and 1-hour rolling budgets per tenant with configurable soft/hard thresholds
When soft threshold exceeded, routing reduces spot preference gradually over a 60-180s decay window instead of immediate cutover
When hard threshold reached, further spot allocations are blocked; on-demand requests allowed up to reserved headroom percentage
System reserves GPU-class headroom per tenant; headroom honored across regions and does not double-count
Fallback model variants are invoked with a progressive degradation policy (quality-first -> performance-first toggles) and logged in evaluation dashboards
End-to-end e2e smoke against canary tenants shows no >2x latency spike and <5% increase in error-rate during simulated spot evictions
Operational metrics (cost, spot-usage, swap-count, rollback-events) surfaced in console and sampled traces include routing decision reason
design_decisions: Use rolling-window counters (circular buffers) instead of instantaneous budget tokens to capture bursty behavior and allow temporary overshoot control
Preference score is an exponential moving average (EMA) over availability/price signals with configurable half-life per tenant
Separate soft vs hard budget semantics: soft triggers adaptive throttling policies, hard triggers deterministic gating with audit logs
Implement GPU-class headroom as percentage reservations mapped to instance families rather than physical device IDs to keep routing portable across clouds
Fallback model variants are pre-registered with compatibility metadata (max sequence length, tokenizer, latency profile) to enable immediate safe substitution
tradeoffs: Smoothing reduces reactive cost-saving opportunities during sustained market dips (some potential for higher short-term cost) vs preventing oscillation-induced availability problems
Reserving headroom increases baseline cost slightly but reduces risk of large customer-facing SLO regressions on spot evictions
Rolling windows add state and memory overhead in the router; chosen circular buffer size tuned to 1s resolution for 1-hour window to balance accuracy vs footprint
Progressive fallback requires maintaining & testing multiple model variants per deployment which increases CI complexity
tasks: Spec: finalize API for per-tenant budget config and headroom percent (PRD link in 'links')
Runtime: implement rolling-window budget counters in routing service
Runtime: implement EMA-based preference score & decay scheduler
Runtime: enforce soft/hard thresholds with telemetry hooks
Runtime: add GPU-class reservation layer that interacts with allocator
Models: register fallback variants and build variant-compatibility matrix
Observability: dashboard for spend pacer metrics and traces
E2E: create canary pipeline and chaos tests simulating spot evictions
Docs/Console: expose tenant knobs and recommended defaults
comments: 2025-02-19 - Aisha Patel: Drafted initial problem statement and proposed pacer approach. Shared with runtime and cost-ops for early feedback.
2025-02-21 - Erin Zhang (runtime): Reviewed rolling-window counters. Concern: memory footprint if we keep 1s resolution for many tenants. Suggested 5s buckets with interpolation for >10k tenants.
2025-02-24 - Miguel Torres: Implemented prototype EMA preference scorer and unit tests. Pushed branch: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4287
2025-02-25 - CostOps (notes): Recommend default soft threshold at 60% of committed spend and hard at 95% for Dedicated customers. For hosted tenants, defaults 40%/90% to encourage early throttling.
2025-02-27 - Design review: tradeoff accepted to use family-level headroom mapping to ensure cross-cloud consistency. Need extra test coverage for family-to-sku translation.
2025-03-01 - QA: Found an edge case where headroom accounting double-counts when tenant uses multi-region replication. Adding atomic reservation step to allocator to fix.
2025-03-03 - Miguel Torres: Updated routing logic to use 5s bucket resolution and introduced background compaction to bound memory. Beginning canary rollout to 3 tenants.
2025-03-03 - PM note (Ravi Kapoor): Add rollout checklist item to verify console knobs are visible to account admins and that audit logs include reason codes for regulatory customers.
